title: Arjuna's Charioteer
body:
Arjuna's Charioteer

As the drums of war began to sound across the land, both sides recognised that the alignment of Sree Krishna would determine the fate of the war. Learning that Krishna had returned to Dwaraka, both Duryodhana and Arjuna set off in haste to secure his alliance. They reached Sree Krishna's palace on the very same day. Duryodhana arrived first, while Sree Krishna was asleep, and took his seat proudly at the head of the bed. Arjuna entered shortly after and stood humbly at the foot of the bed, with hands clasped in reverence.
Upon waking, Sree Krishna's eyes first fell upon Arjuna, who stood at his feet. Turning, he beheld Duryodhana seated at his head. Duryodhana immediately claimed preference, arguing that he had arrived first and that tradition demanded he be shown priority. Krishna smiled and replied that while Duryodhana had arrived first, he had seen Arjuna first upon waking. Therefore, his obligation to render assistance was equal to both.
Sree Krishna offered a choice between two distinct forms of aid: on one side stood his massive, undefeated army, the Narayani Sainya, composed of thousands of veteran Yadava warriors; on the other side stood Krishna himself, alone, unarmed, and pledged not to wield any weapon or participate in actual fighting. Because custom gave the younger man first choice, Krishna offered the choice to Arjuna first.
Without a moment's hesitation, Arjuna bowed reverently and chose Sree Krishna, even if he remained unarmed. Duryodhana could hardly contain his joy at what he perceived as Arjuna's foolishness, and gladly chose the invincible Narayani Sainya. When Duryodhana departed, Sree Krishna smiled and asked Arjuna why he had chosen a weaponless non-combatant over a mighty army. Arjuna replied that he had no doubt of his own ability to defeat the enemy, but he yearned for Sree Krishna's presence to guide his chariot and illuminate his path on the battlefield.

यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन ।
न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम् ।।

Translation: "I am the generating seed of all existences. There is no being—moving or unmoving—that can exist without Me." — Verse Gita X-39
